gaps.quote: The new algorithm reduces its Fourier transforms to polynomial products
gaps.note: The reader has not been taught the discrete Fourier transform. The page neither explains Fourier transforms nor links them to a wiki page, yet it says the saving comes from the transforms.

gaps.quote: The new algorithm therefore never calls itself on smaller inputs, so no recurrence is needed for it
gaps.note: This does not follow and is too strong. That the multiplier calls do not invoke the improved theorem recursively (paper lines 328-329) only shows the subroutine is not the improved algorithm. It does not show that the algorithm has no recursion. The paper's saving comes from recursive calls inside its networks and layers: a call at parameter mf uses s calls at parameter f with s/W<m (paper lines 118-175), and it analyses explicit recurrences (lines 1317-1353, 2393, 4914-4920). So the algorithm does have recurrences, only not through the integer multiplier. The correct statement is that the multiplier calls add no recursion, and their costs are charged separately (line 4917).
